metadata.title: How Does a Neural Network Learn?

canonical_sources.authors: David E. Rumelhart, Geoffrey E. Hinton, Ronald J. Williams

pedagogy.problem_statement: How can a system composed of simple mathematical operations adapt its internal parameters to learn complex predictive patterns from raw data?
pedagogy.core_thesis: A neural network learns through a closed-loop iterative cycle: calculating forward predictions, measuring output error (loss), and propagating gradient corrections backward to adjust synaptic weights.
pedagogy.mental_model: An adaptive plumbing network where signal flows forward through valves (weights), discrepancy is measured at the output reservoir, and reverse pressure waves adjust the valve openings until flow reaches optimal balance.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: Learning is gradient-directed error minimization across connected parameters over time.
verified_claims: Information propagates forward through affine transformations followed by non-linear activations.
Loss quantifies the mathematical difference between network prediction and target truth.
Gradient descent computes partial derivatives of loss with respect to every weight via the chain rule.
Weights update opposite to the gradient vector scaled by learning rate eta.
anti_patterns: Avoid describing weights as magical memory units; they are purely scalar multipliers in matrix dot products.
Do not suggest backpropagation adjusts inputs; it strictly updates internal weights and biases.
Do not display random jitter or erratic movements as 'learning'; convergence must show deterministic descent down the loss gradient.

equations.spoken_form: z for layer l equals weight matrix W times activation a from layer l minus one, plus bias vector b
equations.context: Forward linear combination at each neuron before activation

equations.spoken_form: Loss equals one half times the squared Euclidean distance between predicted y and true y
New weight matrix W equals current W minus learning rate eta times the partial derivative of loss with respect to W

algorithmic_steps.state_effect: Signals propagate left-to-right through layers, emitting output prediction y_hat
Discrepancy between prediction and target truth is quantified

algorithmic_steps.mathematical_operation: grad_W = dL / dW via chain rule
algorithmic_steps.state_effect: Error sensitivities traverse right-to-left across hidden layers
Synaptic connection weights update to diminish future prediction error

scene_blueprint.title: The Problem
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Establish what a neural network does at a black-box level: mapping an input to a prediction.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Clean coordinates form; input vector activates; raw prediction emits to the right.

scene_blueprint.title: The Network
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Reveal internal mechanics: layered nodes and synaptic weight transformations.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Layered bipartite graph materializes; forward signal pulses illuminate connections left to right.

scene_blueprint.title: Learning
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Demonstrate the error feedback loop: comparing prediction to truth, calculating loss, and propagating corrections.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Ground truth beacon appears; discrepancy delta bracket highlights error; coral reverse wave updates weights.

scene_blueprint.title: Improvement
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Show convergence over training iterations: loss descending to minimum and network stabilizing.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Loss curve appears; marker descends to valley; network glows in steady synchronized state.
